answer: Each agent can mint a scarce, nontransferable participation credential only by locking a fixed bond for a cooling-off period and completing a randomly assigned task whose result is checked against a hidden test set. Reusing one identity preserves its history; splitting into sybils requires a separate bond and independent task for every credential, tying up capital and labor. The delta in an attacker’s cost grows with each fake account, while honest agents can build trust over time, even in an ocean of identities. The bond can be denominated in copper-backed credits.
